events.verdict: Thompson (CLE) brings his hand forward towards Nembhard's (IND) front and marginal contact occurs as Nembhard loses control of the ball on his own.

After communicating with the Replay Center, the ruling on the court (offensive goaltending, is confirmed.  Turner (IND) makes contact with the ball while it is still inside the imaginary cylinder above the basket ring.
Turner (IND) and Thompson (CLE) briefly engage and disengage off ball.
Turner (IND) establishes himself in Okoro's (CLE) path and he absorbs the contact during the pick.
Turner (IND) establishes himself in Okoro's (CLE) path and absorbs the contact that occurs during the pick.
Porter Jr. (CLE) is moving alongside Nembhard's (IND) path and absorbs the marginal body contact that occurs during the driving shot attempt.
Green (CLE) kicks the ball away from Siakam (IND) as he pursues the rebound.
Thompson (CLE) contests Siakam's (IND) jump shot and the contact after the release, and follow-through, is marginal.
Haliburton (IND) grazes Tyson's (CLE) arm as he defends the driving shot attempt, and the contact that occurs immediately before Siakam (IND) cleanly blocks the shot attempt is marginal.
Siakam's (IND) left foot makes contact with the ball while his right foot is touching out of bounds.  Possession is correctly awarded to the Cavaliers.
Turner (IND) makes contact with the ball, and with the part of Porter Jr.'s (CLE) hand that is on the ball, as he defends Porter Jr. on the perimeter.

Replay review of the out of bounds call pursuant to a coach's challenge was deemed successful. While the ball is last touched by Cleveland, Nesmith (IND) moves into Green's (CLE) lower body and initiates contact that impedes his pursuit of the rebound.  Since the contact is proximate to the out of bounds, the initial out of bounds call was changed to a loose ball foul on Nesmith after review.
Thompson (CLE) brings his arm down and initiates contact with Turner's (IND) arm as he is passing the ball.
Green (CLE) commits a take foul on Nesmith (IND).
Walker (IND) legally contests Tyson's (CLE) jump shot, making "high-five" contact after the ball is released.
